model_annotations.Chinese:
The figure presents a comparison of per-output and per-layer perplexity at different sparsity rates. 

The horizontal axis represents the sparsity rates, ranging from 10% to 80% in 10% increments. The vertical axis represents perplexity values on a logarithmic scale. 

Two sets of bars are shown: Per-Output and Per-Layer. The Per-Output bars are one color, and the Per-Layer bars are another color. At 10% sparsity, both types of bars have similar perplexity values around 5.70. As sparsity increases, both types of bars increase in height, but the Per-Layer bars are shorter than the Per-Output bars at lower sparsity rates. At higher sparsity rates, the Per-Layer bars are significantly shorter than the Per-Output bars, with values at 886.10 for Per-Layer and 534.42 for Per-Output at 80% sparsity. No bars are visually emphasized. The bars are ordered by sparsity rate from left to right in increasing order.
